Workouts, heatmap, weight, calendar, and backup
Create or select a workout plan. Tap Start workout, complete your sets and exercises, then finish the workout.
On Overview, the muscle heatmap shows which muscle groups you trained and how recently. Colors come from completed workouts with finished sets assigned to a muscle group.
On Overview, tap a day in the calendar to log body weight. Saved measurements appear in the body-weight chart.
The Overview calendar marks days with body weight, workouts, and planned workouts. Tap a day to see the details. Completed workouts and weight entries also appear in Journal.

In Settings, export a backup of structured training data and progress photos. Health Connect readings are not included. Restore replaces the current data with the file. Older JSON backups restore structured data and leave progress photos already on this device in place. This cannot be undone for the data in the file.

Health Connect is optional. In Settings, you can allow the app to read recent activity (steps and exercise sessions) and recovery trends (resting heart rate, HRV, and sleep duration). The app does not write those readings, does not upload them, does not save them in its database, and does not include them in backup or export. Only recent days are shown. Turning that access off does not delete workouts or body data stored in the app. The rest of the app works without Health Connect.
This describes how the current alpha of Strict handles information. It only covers behavior that exists in this version of the app.

Strict stores the training data you enter on this device: body-weight measurements, body measurements, progress photos, exercises, workout plans, scheduled workouts, workout sessions and completed sets, appearance settings, and in-app onboarding progress. A starter exercise catalog may be created locally on first launch. Health Connect access is optional. When you grant it, the app reads recent activity (steps and exercise sessions) and recovery trends (resting heart rate, HRV, and sleep duration). Those readings are shown in the app and are not saved in Strict\'s database.

This data is stored in local app storage on your device (a local database, private photo files, and local settings). Progress photos are not added to your public gallery. Ordinary use does not create an account. Joining the Founding Tester program creates a Strict account from Google sign-in. The limited workout metadata described under What is sent is also stored by the Strict service for that program.

The app does not include analytics, advertising, or crash reporting. Ordinary use does not upload workouts, body weight, progress photos, or Health Connect readings, and it does not write activity or recovery data back to Health Connect. Joining the Founding Tester program sends a Google ID token to the Strict service to open a Strict account, then sends an enrollment request. After you join, each qualifying workout you finish in Strict sends limited metadata: when it was completed, its date, its name, elapsed duration, how many exercises and completed sets it had, and whether it came from a template or used external load. That upload does not include exercise names, individual sets, reps, weights, notes, body weight, photos, or Health Connect data. Your written Tester Report feedback is sent when you submit it.

You can export a backup of structured data and progress photos, and restore a backup you choose. Health Connect readings are not included. You pick the destination or source file. If you save a file to cloud storage or share it, that copy is outside this app. Restore replaces the current data with the backup you select. Older JSON backups leave progress photos already on this device in place.

Send feedback opens your email app with a draft addressed to %1$s. The draft includes app version, Android version, and device manufacturer/model. The app does not send the email itself. You decide whether to send it. Anything you send is then handled by your email provider.

You can delete individual measurements, progress photos, and workouts in the app. Revoking Health Connect access does not delete workouts or body data stored in the app. Uninstalling Strict or clearing the app\'s data removes the locally stored data. This app does not participate in Android cloud backup or device-to-device transfer of its data.

This alpha does not embed analytics, advertising, or other third-party data-collection services. File pickers and email apps you use belong to your device and are not controlled by Strict. Health Connect is the on-device health store. Strict reads activity and recovery trends only after you grant access. It does not send those readings to a Strict service. Joining the Founding Tester program uses Google sign-in. The app sends that Google ID token only to the Strict service. Ordinary use does not use Google sign-in.
